record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: What is the internal structure of exotic charm states such as Ds0*(2317), X(3872), and Tcc+: are they molecular states, orbital excited resonances, tetraquarks, pentaquarks, or something else, and what experimental constraints on charm-hadron strong interactions are needed for models to distinguish these interpretations?

evidence.quote: The study of interactions involving charm mesons has gained significant interest after the observation of the charm-strange meson D*s0(2317), whose mass lies significantly below the quark model predictions, preventing its accommodation in simple constituent quark models.
Also other exotic states, like the X(3872), the T+cc, cannot yet be unambiguously interpreted.

The current models, lacking any experimental constraints about the charm hadrons strong interaction, are not yet able to provide a solid answer about the nature of exotic objects leaving different interpretations, like molecular states, orbital excited resonance states, and tetraquarks/pentaquarks, still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the exotic charm hadrons D*_{s0}(2317), X(3872), and T_{cc}^+, observed as narrow resonances containing one or more charm quarks whose masses lie close to two-meson thresholds (DK for D*_{s0}(2317), D D̄* for X(3872), and DD* for T_{cc}^+) and which do not fit naturally into the predictions of the conventional constituent quark model for q\bar q or qqq states. Several competing internal-structure hypotheses have been proposed for such states: (i) hadronic molecular states bound by meson exchange between two ordinary mesons, (ii) conventional but orbitally excited q\bar q resonances, (iii) compact tetraquark configurations of the form (qq)(\bar q\bar q) bound by colour forces between diquark and antidiquark clusters, (iv) pentaquark-type configurations, or (v) mixtures of such components with possible q\bar q cores.

Determine the actual internal structure of each of D*_{s0}(2317), X(3872), and T_{cc}^+ within QCD, and identify the set of experimental observables of charm-hadron strong interactions (for example, charm-meson scattering lengths and effective ranges with light hadrons, line shapes near thresholds, production yields and momentum correlations of charm-hadron pairs in heavy-ion or pp collisions) that are sufficient to discriminate decisively between the molecular, conventional excited q\bar q, compact tetraquark, pentaquark, and mixed interpretations.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and experimental studies (LHCb Tcc+ analysis 2022, ongoing CERN heavy-ion programs, and theoretical work modeling D*_{s0}(2317) as a DK molecule and X(3872) as a possible mixture of molecule and c\bar c core) show that the internal structure of these exotic charm states remains unsettled. Competing molecular, compact-tetraquark, and mixed interpretations all remain viable, and additional experimental constraints on charm-hadron strong interactions are still required to distinguish them. The problem is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Study of the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc+
status_evidence.snippet: The structure of the new tetraquark could be a D*+ and a D0 meson bound by exchange of colour-neutral objects, or a colour-charged cc 'diquark' tightly bound to up and down antiquarks.
status_evidence.claim: Internal structure of Tcc+ remains ambiguous between molecular and compact tetraquark interpretations.

status_evidence.title: DK, DDK, and DDDK molecules — understanding the nature of Ds0*(2317)
status_evidence.snippet: The DK interaction in isospin zero is strongly attractive and the Ds0*(2317) can be described as a DK molecular state.
status_evidence.claim: Molecular interpretation of Ds0*(2317) is supported but not exclusive; tetraquark interpretations also persist.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Ds0*(2317) as a 0+ tetraquark state from QCD sum rules
status_evidence.snippet: Ds0*(2317) revisited as a 0+ tetraquark state via QCD sum rules.
status_evidence.claim: Tetraquark interpretation of Ds0*(2317) remains under active consideration.
